es-nasa-energy.title: NASA Earth Observatory, Climate and Earth's Energy Budget
es-nasa-energy.notes: Incoming shortwave, reflected albedo, outgoing infrared, global versus surface budgets; educational overview and approximate climatological numbers.

es-ipcc-energy.title: IPCC AR6 Working Group I, Chapter 7, The Earth's Energy Budget, Climate Feedbacks and Climate Sensitivity (2021)
es-ipcc-energy.notes: Present-day energy flows; feedbacks including water vapor, cloud, ice and radiative forcing; uncertainty and ocean heat uptake.

es-ceres-program.title: NASA Langley Research Center, CERES program
es-ceres-program.notes: Satellite observations of reflected solar and emitted thermal radiation; calibration and energy-budget interpretation.

es-state-climate-2024.title: State of the Climate in 2024, Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society, Earth Radiation Budget section (2025)
es-state-climate-2024.notes: CERES-based Earth radiation budget and documented positive recent energy imbalance; particular values are time-dependent.

es-noaa-winds.title: NOAA JetStream, Global Atmospheric Circulations
es-noaa-winds.notes: Coriolis, Hadley/Ferrel/polar circulation cells and their simplified structure, shifting rain and pressure belts.

es-noaa-jets.title: NOAA JetStream, The Jet Stream
es-noaa-jets.notes: Temperature gradients, upper-air jets, seasonal shifts, storms and variable wave structure.

es-noaa-rossby.title: NOAA JetStream, Longwaves and Shortwaves
es-noaa-rossby.notes: Large-scale Rossby waves and their relationship to jet-stream meanders and the development of weather systems.

es-noaa-radiosonde.title: NOAA National Weather Service, Radiosonde Observation
es-noaa-radiosonde.notes: Balloon-borne radiosonde measurements of pressure, temperature, humidity, wind and vertical atmospheric structure.

es-metoffice-circulation.title: UK Met Office, Global Circulation Patterns
es-metoffice-circulation.notes: ITCZ, Hadley cell, subtropical descent, midlatitude westerlies and monsoon-like seasonal geographic influences.

es-ferrel-eddy.title: Liu and Alexander, Atmospheric Bridge, Oceanic Tunnel, and Global Climatic Teleconnections, Reviews of Geophysics (2007)
es-ferrel-eddy.notes: Section 2.1.2: Ferrel cells as eddy-driven, thermally indirect mean circulations; midlatitude storms carry poleward energy.

es-thermal-wind.title: University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee, Synoptic Meteorology I: Thermal Wind Balance (teaching notes)
es-thermal-wind.notes: Derivation and interpretation of vertical geostrophic shear and horizontal layer-mean temperature gradients.

es-ipcc-water.title: IPCC AR6 Working Group I, Chapter 8, Water Cycle Changes (2021)
es-ipcc-water.notes: Global humidity response, precipitation energy constraints, water cycle variability and global versus regional patterns.

es-usgs-water.title: US Geological Survey Water Science School, Water Cycle
es-usgs-water.notes: Storage versus flow; evaporation, precipitation, transpiration, infiltration, runoff and human influence.

es-usgs-groundwater.title: US Geological Survey, Ground Water and Surface Water: A Single Resource, Circular 1139
es-usgs-groundwater.notes: Gaining and losing streams; hydraulic gradients, shallow groundwater and flow effects of pumping.

es-usgs-tracers.title: US Geological Survey, Circular 1139, Box G: Environmental Tracers
es-usgs-tracers.notes: Hydrogen and oxygen isotopes, tritium, radon and chemical tracers for residence, origin and flow pathways.

es-nasa-grace.title: NASA Earth Observatory, The Gravity of Water
es-nasa-grace.notes: GRACE twin-satellite gravity measurement and its relationship to water-storage changes.

es-usgs-grace-limit.title: Castellazzi et al., Assessing Groundwater Depletion and Dynamics using GRACE and InSAR: Potential and Limitations (2016)
es-usgs-grace-limit.notes: GRACE spatial averaging limits and separation from local aquifer behavior; complementarity with InSAR.

es-noaa-currents.title: NOAA National Ocean Service, What Is a Current?
es-noaa-currents.notes: Wind, tides, and density differences as ocean-current drivers.

es-noaa-boundary.title: NOAA National Ocean Service, Boundary Currents
es-noaa-boundary.notes: Western boundary intensification and the Gulf Stream as an example of western boundary circulation.

es-ipcc-ocean.title: IPCC AR6 Working Group I, Chapter 9, Ocean, Cryosphere and Sea Level Change (2021)
es-ipcc-ocean.notes: Ocean heat uptake, Southern Ocean exchange and water-mass formation, thermal expansion and observed sea-level change.

es-noaa-ocean-exploration.title: NOAA Ocean Exploration, What Causes Ocean Currents?
es-noaa-ocean-exploration.notes: Surface wind-driven flow, Coriolis, vertical circulation, density-driven deep flow and topographic effects.

es-noaa-upwelling.title: NOAA Fisheries, Oceanography of the Northern California Current Study Area
es-noaa-upwelling.notes: California/Oregon/Washington upwelling, seasonal wind variability, cold nutrient-rich source water and biological production.

es-noaa-argo.title: NOAA Atlantic Oceanographic and Meteorological Laboratory, Argo Program
es-noaa-argo.notes: Argo history, measurement depths, global temperature/salinity profiles and Deep Argo development.

es-whoi-argo.title: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, How Do the Argo Floats Work?
es-whoi-argo.notes: Park-and-profile 10-day cycle, conductivity-temperature-pressure and satellite communication.

es-ucar-argo.title: UCAR Climate Data Guide, Argo Ocean Temperature and Salinity Profiles
es-ucar-argo.notes: Observing-system strengths, vertical profiles and caveats about deep ocean, sea ice and coastal sampling.

es-ipcc-carbon.title: IPCC AR6 Working Group I, Chapter 5, Global Carbon and other Biogeochemical Cycles and Feedbacks (2021)
es-ipcc-carbon.notes: Observed anthropogenic carbon budget partition in 2010-2019, isotopic and inventory attribution, carbon sinks and feedbacks.

es-scripps-keeling.title: Scripps Institution of Oceanography, The Keeling Curve
es-scripps-keeling.notes: Mauna Loa measurements began in 1958; seasonal oscillation and long-term atmospheric CO2 trend.

es-fluxnet.title: FLUXNET, About the FLUXNET Network
es-fluxnet.notes: Eddy covariance observes carbon, water and energy fluxes at ecosystem-atmosphere interface; local footprint and gap processing matter.

es-fluxnet2015.title: Pastorello et al., The FLUXNET2015 dataset and the ONEFlux processing pipeline, Scientific Data (2020)
es-fluxnet2015.notes: Flux measurements, gap filling, separating ecosystem respiration from photosynthesis, and uncertainty estimates.

es-oco2.title: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, OCO-2 Measurement Approach
es-oco2.notes: Satellite XCO2 is inferred from reflected sunlight absorption; carbon sources/sinks require inverse atmospheric transport modeling.

es-noaa-acid.title: NOAA Ocean Acidification Program, What is Ocean Acidification?
es-noaa-acid.notes: Seawater carbonic acid/bicarbonate/carbonate chemistry, pH and monitoring.

es-nasa-carbon.title: NASA Earth Observatory, The Carbon Cycle
es-nasa-carbon.notes: Fast biological and slow geological carbon pathways, silicate weathering, sediment transport, rock formation.

es-walker-weathering.title: Walker, Hays, and Kasting, A negative feedback mechanism for the long-term stabilization of Earth's surface temperature, JGR (1981)
es-walker-weathering.notes: Original 1981 hypothesis for long-term temperature-dependent silicate weathering feedback; explicitly qualified in original abstract.

es-nature-himalaya.title: Märki et al., An unshakable carbon budget for the Himalaya, Nature Geoscience (2021)
es-nature-himalaya.notes: 2015 Gorkha earthquake catchment; study distinguishes organic and inorganic pathways and reports muted integrated basin budget response.

es-nsidc-seaice.title: National Snow and Ice Data Center, Science of Sea Ice
es-nsidc-seaice.notes: Sea-ice formation, albedo, melt ponds and ocean-ice energy exchanges.

es-nsidc-floating.title: National Snow and Ice Data Center, Does Sea Ice Melt Raise Sea Level? (2025)
es-nsidc-floating.notes: Archimedean displacement with subtle freshwater/seawater density correction; direct effect very small.

es-nsidc-shelves.title: National Snow and Ice Data Center, The Science of Ice Shelves
es-nsidc-shelves.notes: Grounding line, buttressing and documented glacier acceleration after Larsen B collapse in 2002.

es-nasa-ice-sheets.title: NASA Science, Ice Sheets, Earth Indicator
es-nasa-ice-sheets.notes: Satellite gravimetry record of mass loss from Greenland and Antarctica with period-specific updates.

es-jpl-grace.title: NASA JPL, GRACE Follow-On
es-jpl-grace.notes: Gravity variations indicate changing mass distributions including ice, soil water and oceans.

es-nasa-ice-altimetry.title: NASA Earth Observatory, Taking a Measure of Sea Level Rise: Ice Height
es-nasa-ice-altimetry.notes: What radar and laser altimetry measure about surface elevation, including snow penetration and coverage limits.

es-usgs-glacier-balance.title: USGS, Compiled Input Data and Glacier-Wide Mass Balances (data release, updated 2026)
es-usgs-glacier-balance.notes: Field stake and snow observations, water equivalent mass balance and geodetic calibration for glaciers.

es-usgs-sediment.title: USGS Water Science School, Sediment and Suspended Sediment (updated 2026)
es-usgs-sediment.notes: Suspended sediment, deposition and the possibility of large storm contributions to annual sediment discharge.

es-usgs-fluvial.title: USGS, Fluvial Sediments: Source, Transportation, Deposition, and Measurement (1963)
es-usgs-fluvial.notes: Suspended sediment, bedload, sediment sources, transport and measurement challenges.

es-usgs-landslides.title: USGS, What is a Landslide and What Causes One?
es-usgs-landslides.notes: Landslide motion classes, gravity, material strength and common hydrological/geophysical triggers.

es-nps-slopes.title: National Park Service, Landslide Hazards
es-nps-slopes.notes: Pore pressure, slope saturation, lateral support and earthquake-triggered mass movement.
